title: Allocation of Rent Discounts Across a Lessee's Safe Deposit Box Rentals
content:
Rent discounts on Safe Deposit Boxes are allocated across the whole of a customer's rentals rather than granted separately on each box. Which rental a discount reaches, and which single discount is then applied to it, are settled as follows.

## The discount for an active checking relationship

Holding an active Premier Checking or Private Client Checking account earns the relationship discount on one rental only. That rental is the customer's active or past-due rental with the highest annual rent before discount; where two such rentals carry the same annual rent before discount, it is the one whose lease began earlier.

## The discount for age, and the discount for employment

The age discount applies where the lessee is at least 65 whole years old on the rent due date. The employment discount applies where the lessee is an active PCB employee. Each of these may apply to every one of the lessee's rentals.

## Which discount is applied to a rental

The discounts a lessee qualifies for on the rent due date are the relationship discount for each active checking tier held, the age discount and the employment discount, each with its percent. Of those available to a given rental, only the largest percent is applied. Discounts never add together, and the smaller percents fall away.

## When the discount is settled

The discount is fixed when that year's rent is charged. A holding opened or closed later in the same rental year does not change it.

## A worked allocation on hypothetical facts

Suppose a lessee holds three rentals of Safe Deposit Boxes: an active rental whose annual rent before discount is $138.00, a past-due rental whose annual rent before discount is $97.75, and a waitlisted rental not yet leased whose size would carry $71.50. Suppose the lessee holds an active Premier Checking account.

The relationship discount reaches one rental only, and the candidates are the active and past-due rentals. Of those two, the higher annual rent before discount is $138.00, so the relationship discount attaches to that rental. The past-due rental takes no relationship discount. The waitlisted rental is not a candidate at all, being neither active nor past due. The three amounts named here are hypothetical inputs.

Suppose instead the two candidate rentals each carried $120.00 before discount. The tie is settled by the earlier lease start date, and the relationship discount attaches to the rental whose lease began first.

If the same lessee were also at least 65 on the rent due date, the age discount would be available to each of the rentals in its own right; on the rental that also has the relationship discount available to it, the larger of the two percents alone is applied.
